bib.title: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention". Yan Wang (project lead), Qifan Zhang, Jiachen Yu, Tian Liang, Dongyang Ma (equal contribution), Xiang Hu, Zibo Lin, Chunyang Li, Zhichao Wang, Miao Peng, Nuo Chen, Jia Li, Yujiu Yang, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu. Affiliations: Tencent, HKUST-GZ, Tsinghua, independent. Preprint, arXiv 2606.09079v3, cs.LG, 20 Jul 2026. Ledger title "Lookahead Sparse Attention" is the method name.

COVERAGE: Full. I read 41,181 of 41,181 extracted chars (12 pages), including the limitations section and the references. The paper has no appendices. I did not run the figures script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Central claim: LSA keeps only query-critical compressed KV chunks (CSA) on the GPU and offloads the rest to CPU. A small standalone "Memory Indexer" predicts which chunks are needed over the next τ decode steps. Average GPU KV falls to 13.5% of full, with accuracy held or slightly raised.
  number: 13.5% of baseline KV; +0.6 absolute accuracy
  setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbone, averaged over the LongBench-v2, LongMemEval and RULER rows of Table 1. Baseline is unmodified DS-V4-Flash with a full KV cache.
  quote: "FM-DS-V4 consumes merely 13.5% of the baseline GPU memory footprint—representing an average 86.5% reduction in KV cache storage—while actually improving overall performance to 77.5% (+0.6% absolute margin over DS-V4-Flash)."
  where: Sec 3.2, p.9-10
- Claim: Table 1 gives the per-benchmark accuracy and GPU KV size.
  number: Average 76.9 (0.93 GB) for DS-V4-Flash vs 77.5 (0.10 GB) for FM-DS-V4, 33.3 (0.04 GB) for Recency Only, 38.7 (0.12 GB) for Random 10%.
  setup: Columns are DS-V4-Flash, FM-DS-V4, Recency Only, Random 10%. Context lengths run from 46K to 512K.
  quote: "LongBench-v2-L(493K) 68.1 (1.80 GB)70.0(0.18 GB) 54.3 (0.04 GB) 46.9 (0.22 GB)"
  where: Table 1, p.9
  Other rows, as DS-V4-Flash vs FM-DS-V4:
  - LongBench-v2-S (46K): 68.9 vs 70.2
  - LongBench-v2-M (179K): 67.6 vs 68.9
  - LongMemEval-S (125K): 80.6 vs 82.0
  - LongMemEval-M (500K): 39.3 vs 40.2
  - RULER 64K: 94.7 vs 95.0
  - RULER 128K: 94.3 vs 93.2 (FM lower)
  - RULER 256K: 90.5 vs 88.2 (FM lower)
  - RULER 512K: 88.3 vs 89.6
- Claim: At 1M context, GPU KV falls 90% and per-decode-token compute falls to 0.30x.
  number: KV 3.73 to 0.37 GB; 118.9 to 35.4 GFLOP/token
  setup: Measured from sglang deployment logs on an 8×H20 server. Figure 1 also gives 256K and 512K values.
  quote: "At 1M context, per-decode-token compute drops from 118.9 to 35.4 GFLOP (0.30×) while GPU KV cache shrinks by 90% (3.73→0.37 GB). KV cache Overhead and FLOPs are measured via sglang deployment logs on an 8×H20 GPU server."
  where: Fig 1 caption, p.1
  Fig 1 values:
  - KV at 256K: 0.94 to 0.09 GB
  - KV at 512K: 1.87 to 0.18 GB
  - GFLOP/token at 256K: 50.8 to 28.8 (0.57x)
  - GFLOP/token at 512K: 73.5 to 31.0 (0.42x)
- Claim: 2.8x aggregate throughput and 2.7x concurrency in PD-disaggregated serving on 8×H20.
  number: 2.8x; 2.7x
  setup: Stated only in the abstract, intro, Fig 1 title and conclusion. No table, batch size, or baseline serving configuration is given in the body.
  quote: "translating into2.8× aggregate throughput and 2.7× concurrency gainsin PD-disaggregated serving on 8×H20 GPUs."
  where: Abstract, p.1
- Claim: A motivating observation is that most long requests need only recent context.
  number: over 90% of requests with contexts over 64K tokens resolve from the last 8K tokens
  setup: "Real-world inference logs". Source, size and the definition of "accurately resolved" are not given.
  quote: "over 90% of user requests with contexts longer than 64K tokens can be accurately resolved using only the last 8K tokens."
  where: Sec 1, p.2
- Claim: The indexer trains in about one H20 GPU hour without loading the backbone.
  number: ~1 H20 GPU hour; ~500 runs in a week on 8×H20; trainable layers under 0.1% of parameters; about 10,000 documents of 16K to 512K tokens
  setup: Dual-encoder trained only on the query side. Historical compressed indexer keys are frozen and pre-computed offline. Labels come from the frozen DS-V4-Flash.
  quote: "the entire Memory Indexer converges elegantly withina single H20 GPU hour."
  where: Sec 2.3, p.6
- Claim: A 3-layer indexer ensemble is the chosen operating point.
  number: layers 10, 12, 20, combined by OR-union at threshold ≥0.5. An 8-layer setup (layers 6 to 20) fetches 30% to 49% of historical compressed entries.
  quote: "an 8-layer ensemble triggers an excessively loose context recall mask, fetching up to 30%–49% of historical compressed KV entries into the GPU memory"
  where: Sec 2.4, p.6
- Claim: Label construction uses cross-layer majority voting.
  number: p=0.6 nucleus per layer; θ=3 of L=21 CSA layers; the naive top-k union gives ~10,000 positives per window, filtered to ~100–1,000
  quote: "An entry is officially recognized as a core active entryAgolden i if and only if it secures consensus backing from at leastθlayers (we setθ= 3)"
  where: Sec 2.2, p.4-5
- Claim: Recency Only and Random 10% collapse on retrieval-heavy tasks.
  number: LongMemEval-S 19.2 and 20.1 vs FM 82.0; RULER 512K 18.8 and 27.2 vs 89.6
  quote: see Table 1 rows above. The authors say LongBench-v2 stays moderate because HCA layers plus the 8K window are retained in all variants.
  where: Table 1; Sec 3.2, p.10
- Claim: Serving mechanics.
  number: recall runs every τ=64 steps; the out-of-graph CUDA-graph side band is "approximately 50× faster than the non-CUDA-graph version"; recalled entries materialise at step t+1 (zero decode stall)
  setup: P-server is unmodified. Prefill exports full KV into the D-server's host pinned memory. The GPU resident set is HCA (128:1), CSA for the last 8K prompt tokens, all decoded-token CSA, index-K for layers 10, 12, 20, plus the recalled subset. Everything else sits in a CPU cold mirror.
  quote: "Because the offloaded history occupies no GPU KV, the per-request footprint drops fromO(context)to O(|C MemComp t |)."
  where: Sec 2.5, p.7-8
- Claim (failure): MRCR breaks.
  number: 76.0% to 48.0%. Oracle top-50% golden chunks still lose about 2%.
  setup: Oracle sweep with DS-V4-Flash attention weights at top 50/25/10% chunks. On LongBench-v2, LongMemEval and RULER, 10% to 25% golden chunks recover baseline.
  quote: "accuracy plummets from the baseline's 76.0% down to adismal 48.0%."
  where: Sec 3.3.2, p.10-11
- Claim (failure): The footprint does not stay constant on context-independent queries.
  number: LongMemEval-S no-context 96.7 (0.46 GB) vs 95.0 (0.06 GB); M no-context 91.2 (1.82 GB) vs 92.5 (0.16 GB). Retained volume grows about 2.5x from 125K to 500K, while the ratio falls to 8.4%.
  quote: "the physical absolute chunk retention volume inflates by approximately2.5×."
  where: Table 2 and Sec 3.3.1, p.10
- Claim (failure): Length generalisation is capped at about 2x the training length.
  number: 2x training context; the released indexer is trained to 512K
  quote: "The indexer safely generalizesup to exactly2× its training context length."
  where: Sec 3.3.3, p.11
  Note: the 1M-context efficiency figures (Fig 1) sit beyond the 512K training range. The paper says validation above that is "untested" and that discriminability is hypothesised to decay past 1M. The paper reports no 1M accuracy.

LIMITS
- Project suspended. τ=64 and the threshold of 0.5 were never ablated, and layer-wise ablation is described as coarse.
- Accuracy tables report single numbers with no variance, seeds or confidence intervals. The "+0.6" average is smaller than several per-row gaps, and FM is lower on RULER 128K (−1.1) and 256K (−2.3).
- "Less is more / attention denoiser" is the authors' interpretation. No experiment isolates a denoising mechanism.
- KV sizes in Table 1 are GPU-resident KV only. CPU DRAM holds the full mirror, and host-to-device recall traffic and PCIe/bandwidth cost are not quantified. Total memory is not reduced.
- The throughput and concurrency figures lack a methodology and a table. No latency numbers are given.
- Benchmarks cover only three suites plus MRCR. No code, math or agentic tasks are reported.
- Authors concede three constraints: frozen keys, shallow dot-product interaction (they suggest ColBERT-style late interaction), and no joint training with the backbone.
- Applies only to DeepSeek-V4-Flash (21 CSA layers).

BUILDS ON
- DeepSeek-AI, DeepSeek-V4 technical report, 2026 [1]: CSA, HCA at 128:1, Lightning Indexer, and the "structural compression spirit".
- Qwen3.5 (Qwen Team, 2026) [2], cited as a comparison for linear-attention hybrids.
- Benchmarks: LongBench v2 (Bai et al., 2025); LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2025); RULER (Hsieh et al., 2024); MRCR via Michelangelo (Vodrahalli et al., 2024).
- DeepSeek-V3 `q_lora_rank` (default 1536) is mentioned; the paper uses 2048.
- Focal loss and BCE are used without citation.
- DeepSeek Sparse Attention and NSA are not cited; the only origin named is DeepSeek-V4's Lightning Indexer.

CODE: none. A "Code" badge appears on the first page, with no link in the extraction.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): LongBench-v2 accuracy by length; GPU KV cache at 256K/512K/1M (−90% each); per-decode-token GFLOP. Shows the memory and compute savings together.
- Fig 2 (p.3): LSA vs CSA pipeline. The Memory Indexer runs every τ steps with a sigmoid and threshold recall from CPU to GPU, then the native top-k.
- Fig 3 (p.8): PD-disaggregated serving, with the CPU cold mirror and CUDA-graph side band.
- Fig 4 (p.9): KV layout across P and D servers; the GPU-resident tiers.
- Table 1 (p.9) is the main result.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean except for garbled math symbols and the figure chart text. No embedded instructions found. Abstract numbers (2.8x, 2.7x) have no corresponding body table.
